May 2026 produced v1 and a research programme around it. A first package and manuscript of 5 May drew a critical review (known results presented as theorems, illustrative instead of measured figures, no code), so the package was rebuilt the next day and released as v1.0.0 on 7 May, with a benchmark run behind its numbers; it was posted to arXiv and submitted to SciPost Physics Codebases. Two research directions were piloted before any theorem was attempted, so that a weak direction would be stopped cheaply: C2, sector-decomposed enclosures with guaranteed error bounds, was killed because the literature already covered it and the pilot gain was 5.2 to 5.5 times against a pre-registered 100 times; C1, Chebyshev-preconditioned Krawczyk verification, passed its pilot on two stacks and exposed an overflow bug on the way. symveig 1.0.0, the implementation work that survived C2, was released on 22 May.

June brought the second arXiv version of v1, the symveig preprint and the first referee report, a reject. Its technical points (residuals suffice, the LAPACK paths share DSYTRD, Hamiltonian construction is excluded) were judged genuine, so instead of a rebuttal (D-04) the project audited its own manuscript and code; both audits confirmed the referee's points and found further defects. The audits ran into July, and their exact days are not recorded.

Two further rejects, on 10 and 21 July, converged on the same diagnosis: the paper claimed generality and covered small dense LAPACK runs. On 13 July the project pivoted (D-03 to D-14): no rebuttal, CERTIFY-ED to be broadened into a general verification substrate, and a complete enumeration of the verification space to come before any engineering plan, so that the plan could not filter the scope the way v1's plan had. After the third reject the writing process changed so that Sarang drafts the load-bearing prose (D-16).
No dated change is recorded for August 2026. The handover of 21 July names Sarang's review of the scope enumeration as the next step; no record of that review is in the archive.

Work resumed on 25 September with Sarang's request for a substantially revised manuscript (D-17). Instead of patching v1, its code was imported as the baseline of a new repository and a v2 verification core was written around the certificate statements S1 to S5 with four statuses (D-18 to D-20), because the referees' central objection was that v1 tested LAPACK instead of establishing something about a result for a declared model.

October 2026 holds most of the recorded changes. The v2 core gained the experiments E0 to E5 and the manuscript ms_v2 (4 to 11 October), and the experiments found bugs of the code itself (the Jordan-Wigner direction, unseeded ARPACK, the below-top probe). After SciPost was dropped on 15 October and a survey of horizons showed that published proofs rest on uncertified ED numbers, the project turned to certifying such proof lemmas (the pyrochlore crown of Kránitz and Penc and the AKLT criteria of Pomata and Wei), added an exact re-check layer and mutation analysis, merged symveig after an audit found its counts unproved, and became one codebase, certify-ed 3.0.0 (17 to 18 October). Writing the appendix proofs against the code on 21 October found two soundness gaps, fixed before the full run; an automated independent review that evening found three input paths that gave a false CERTIFIED and the private address in the history, which led to the history rewrite and to release 3.1.0. The first attempt of the 3.1.0 evidence run failed on Windows-portability defects; the second, from tag `v3.1.0`, is the run the paper cites, and the four known issues found afterwards were recorded instead of rerunning it (D-57). From 23 October a scored expansion roadmap drove Waves 0 and 1 on `dev/3.2`, and from 30 October a completion plan cleared the backlog of new mathematics with derivation documents, machine checks and an independent re-derivation, while Sarang's own check stays pending (D-59).

November completed the 3.2 line. Phase 2 of the completion plan added the C verifier, the scale statements and the remaining derivations, and 3.2.0 was tagged on 4 November so that it could get its own full run (D-60). That run crashed in E4, because the new eight-thread residual ended the process under the memory cap. Version 3.2.1 made the residual single-threaded by default, which changes no bound, and its full run of 5 November completed every step. Against 3.1.0 it shows 10 MISMATCH leaves, each a documented change, and identical certified application results; the manuscript macros were regenerated from it, while the cited version stays 3.1.0 until Sarang decides (D-61). The record of the project archive ends with archive v5 on 6 November; the documentation and the Lean re-verification that followed are in the last section.

One row per version or tag of the code, with the commit (rewritten id where the commit is in the project repository) and the full run made from that version, if any. Versions without a tag are named by their version string. Sources: the sections [1.0.0] to [3.2.1] of `code/certify-ed/CHANGELOG.md`, the tags of the repository (`tools/changelog/tags.tsv`), the run manifests (`tools/changelog/runs.tsv`) and `code/README_code.md`.

After archive v5 the project was documented and re-checked in a separate repository, certify-ed-project, without changing the code or its run records. The documentation, the blog and this changelog were written from the archive, and the mathematics and the certified numbers were re-checked in Lean 4 with Mathlib: an exact checker of the certificates in core Lean, formal proofs of the statements of the derivation documents, and an exact recomputation of the application numbers. The formalization found places where a document states a range, a hypothesis or a reason imprecisely; none changes a certificate, and the code repository received two documentation commits for them. Sources in this section are paths of certify-ed-project and commits of the code bundle in its sources folder.
